reason: Clinical advice, diagnoses, and treatment recommendations must only be provided by qualified medical professionals. This assistant cannot and must not provide clinical guidance.
Medical advice requests including medication prescriptions, dosing, diagnosis interpretation, and treatment options are outside this system's scope and must be refused unconditionally.
Per SOP-BILL-022, billing corrections above $500 require supervisor authorization before adjustment. Auto-routing ensures no large corrections bypass oversight.
Minor billing corrections under $500 can be handled by senior billing staff without escalation per SOP-BILL-022.
TPA claim denials require specialist negotiation with the insurer; the TPA Escalation Manager has authorization to dispute on the hospital's behalf.
Elevated privilege access requests require IT Manager approval to prevent unauthorized access to sensitive systems per the RBAC policy.
Patient complaints require a dedicated Patient Relations officer to manage sensitively and in accordance with the hospital's grievance redressal policy.
Life-critical equipment failures require immediate Biomedical Engineering response per SOP-BIO-002 to ensure patient safety.
Subpoenas and court orders for medical records must be handled exclusively by the Legal & Compliance department to protect patient rights and hospital liability.
Patient safety incidents (falls, medication errors, sentinel events) require immediate Quality & Patient Safety officer involvement per SOP-QA-001.
Waiver requests exceeding 25% of the bill require Finance Director or CEO authorization per SOP-BILL-031.
HIS downtime affects all hospital operations and patient safety; requires immediate IT Emergency Response team activation per SOP-IT-019.
ICU patient transfers require Medical Director sign-off to ensure clinical safety and appropriate receiving ward readiness per SOP-CM-013.
General operational queries that cannot be answered by the knowledge base are routed to the Help Desk for human assistance.
Suspected or confirmed PHI/PII privacy breaches require immediate Data Protection Officer involvement and may have legal/regulatory reporting obligations under HIPAA.
Critical drug stock-outs require immediate Pharmacy Head escalation to activate emergency procurement or therapeutic substitution protocols per SOP-PHARM-005.
Specimen rejection and re-collection must be coordinated through the Laboratory Supervisor to ensure proper re-collection guidance and updated turnaround estimates.
Non-life-critical equipment failures are routed to Biomedical Engineering for scheduling of repair; substitute equipment should be arranged in the interim per SOP-BIO-002.
All reported incidents and near-misses must be reviewed by the Quality & Patient Safety team within 2 hours per SOP-QA-001 to initiate root cause analysis and corrective action.
Bed shortage situations require the Bed Manager to coordinate between wards for reallocation; Operations Manager is involved if multi-department escalation is needed.
Mass Casualty Incident activation requires Emergency Director authority to mobilize hospital-wide MCI response per SOP-EMRG-007; normal operational workflows are suspended.
Procurement requests above $5,000 require Finance Director approval and competitive quotation per SOP-SC-001 to ensure financial governance and vendor transparency.

Adverse drug reactions and drug interactions involve clinical assessment and treatment decisions that must be handled exclusively by the treating physician or clinical pharmacist — outside the scope of this operational assistant.
